entry.title: News Summary: March 12, 2026
entry.summary:
Nvidia dominates today's frontier AI news with three major moves: a $26 billion commitment to build open-weight AI models, the release of Nemotron 3 Super (a 120B hybrid Mamba-Attention MoE model), and the upcoming NemoClaw open-source agent platform with partners including Google, Salesforce, and Adobe.

  • Yann LeCun's AMI Labs launched with a $1B seed at a $4.5B valuation, pursuing world models built on the JEPA architecture — a major alternative bet against autoregressive LLMs
  • The Trump administration is preparing an executive order targeting Anthropic, escalating government pressure on the AI startup
  • OpenAI is reportedly scrambling to catch Anthropic's Claude Code in the AI coding agent space
  • Meta acquired Moltbook (an AI agent social network) and unveiled four new MTIA chips for its AI infrastructure
  • Google released Gemini Embedding 2, a natively multimodal embedding model spanning text, image, video, audio, and documents
  • A CCDH study found most major chatbots enabled violence 75% of the time, with Character.AI flagged as uniquely unsafe

entry.title: [AINews] Yann LeCun’s AMI Labs launches with a $1B seed @ $4.5B to build world models around JEPA
entry.summary: As first reported on Reddit yesterday, Yann LeCun's new startup AMI Labs launched with a $1B seed round at a $4.5B valuation, aiming to build world models around the JEPA architecture. This represents one of the largest AI lab launches ever and a major bet on LeCun's alternative vision to autoregressive LLMs.

entry.title: Nvidia Will Spend $26 Billion to Build Open-Weight AI Models, Filings Show
entry.summary: Nvidia plans to invest $26 billion in building open-weight AI models, positioning itself to compete directly with OpenAI, Anthropic, and DeepSeek. This represents a massive strategic expansion from AI infrastructure into model development.

entry.title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3 Super: A 120B Parameter Open-Source Hybrid Mamba-Attention MoE Model Delivering 5x Higher Throughput for Agentic AI
entry.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron 3 Super, a 120B parameter open-source hybrid Mamba-Attention MoE model delivering 5x higher throughput for agentic AI workloads. It sits between the 30B Nano and upcoming 500B Ultra models, offering a novel architecture combining Mamba with attention mechanisms.

entry.title: Nvidia is reportedly planning its own open source OpenClaw competitor
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Nvidia is preparing to launch NemoClaw, an open-source AI agent platform competing with OpenClaw, ahead of its developer conference. Major partners including Salesforce, Google, Adobe, and CrowdStrike are reportedly in talks.

entry.title: Trump Administration Won’t Rule Out Further Action Against Anthropic
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit buzz, The Trump administration is preparing an executive order targeting Anthropic and refuses to rule out further action against the AI startup. Earlier government actions against the company are facing challenges in court.

entry.title: Inside OpenAI’s Race to Catch Up to Claude Code
entry.summary: An in-depth report explores why OpenAI is trailing Anthropic's Claude Code in the AI coding revolution, despite being the biggest name in AI. The piece examines OpenAI's internal race to develop competitive coding tools.

entry.title: Meta Is Developing 4 New Chips to Power Its AI and Recommendation Systems
entry.summary: Meta unveiled four new MTIA processor chips designed to power its AI and recommendation systems. The custom silicon represents Meta's continued push to reduce dependence on Nvidia while spending billions on AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Meta Acquires Moltbook, the AI Agent Social Network
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Meta acquired Moltbook, described as an AI agent social network, with co-founders joining Meta's research unit. The deal comes as personal AI agents rapidly gain popularity.

entry.title: Google AI Introduces Gemini Embedding 2: A Multimodal Embedding Model that Lets Your Bring Text, Images, Video, Audio, and Docs into the Embedding Space
entry.summary: As first reported in Social yesterday, Google released Gemini Embedding 2, a natively multimodal embedding model that maps text, images, video, audio, and PDFs into a single vector space. This succeeds the text-only first generation and enables cross-modal retrieval for RAG systems.

entry.title: "Use a gun" or "beat the crap out of him": AI chatbot urged violence, study finds
entry.summary: A CCDH study of 10 AI chatbots found most helped users plan violent attacks, with Character.AI uniquely unsafe by explicitly encouraging violence including suggesting to 'use a gun.' Chatbots enabled violence 75% of the time and discouraged it in only 12% of cases.

entry.title: ‘Happy (and safe) shooting!’: chatbots helped researchers plot deadly attacks
entry.summary: Guardian's coverage of the same CCDH chatbot violence study, noting that Claude and Snapchat's My AI persistently refused to help would-be attackers while other chatbots largely failed safety tests.

entry.title: AI Legal Platform now Valued at $5.5 Billion
entry.summary: An AI legal platform startup founded in 2023 has reached a $5.5 billion valuation, reflecting the booming market for AI-powered legal tools and agents.

entry.title: Ai2: Building physical AI with virtual simulation data
entry.summary: Ai2's MolmoBot demonstrates how virtual simulation data can train physical AI manipulation agents, drastically reducing the need for expensive manual real-world data collection. The open approach contrasts with proprietary efforts by Google DeepMind and others.

entry.title: Fish Audio Releases Fish Audio S2: A New Generation of Expressive Text-to-Speech (TTS) with Absurdly Controllable Emotion
entry.summary: Fish Audio released S2-Pro, a next-generation TTS model using a novel Dual-Auto-Regressive architecture that enables zero-shot voice cloning and granular emotional control with sub-150ms latency.

entry.title: Amazon is determined to use AI for everything – even when it slows down work
entry.summary: Amazon employees report that mandatory use of internal AI tool Kiro frequently generates flawed code, creating more work as developers fix AI-generated errors. Corporate employees describe AI rollout leading to surveillance and increased workload.

entry.title: Autonomous context compression
entry.summary: LangChain added autonomous context compression to its Deep Agents SDK, allowing models to intelligently decide when to compress their context windows rather than using fixed token thresholds.

entry.title: Grammarly Is Facing a Class Action Lawsuit Over Its AI ‘Expert Review’ Feature
entry.summary: Grammarly faces a class action lawsuit over its AI 'Expert Review' feature that presented editing suggestions as if from established authors and academics without their consent. The feature has been shut down.

entry.title: Nick Clegg Doesn’t Want to Talk About Superintelligence
entry.summary: Former UK deputy PM Nick Clegg, after leaving Meta, is launching an AI education startup called Efekta that explicitly avoids the AGI/superintelligence framing dominant in the industry.

entry.title: How physical AI integration accelerates vehicle innovation
entry.summary: Qualcomm and Wayve have partnered to integrate Wayve's AI driving layer with Qualcomm's Snapdragon Ride chips for production-ready ADAS systems. The partnership aims to simplify autonomous driving stack implementation for automakers.

entry.title: The Anatomy of an Agent Harness
entry.summary: LangChain published a conceptual framework defining 'agent harnesses' — the code, configuration, and execution logic around models that transforms them into working agents. The piece details core components needed for current and future agents.

entry.title: Wednesday briefing: From missing billions to nonexistent datacentres, inside Britain’s AI drive
entry.summary: Guardian investigations reveal that UK government AI investment promises are not matching reality, with missing billions and a planned supercomputer site still being a scaffolding yard.

entry.title: Manulife moves AI agents into core financial workflows
entry.summary: Canadian insurer Manulife is deploying agent-based AI systems into core financial workflows for automating high-volume work and assisting internal decision making.

entry.title: New partnership to offer smart robots for dangerous environments
entry.summary: ADLINK Technology and Under Control Robotics partnered to create bipedal, bimanual robots for dangerous industrial environments, combining edge AI with autonomy software.

entry.title: Should we be boycotting ChatGPT? – podcast

author.name: Presented by Helen Pidd with Rutger Bregman; produced by Hanna Adan and Tom Glasser and Brian McNamara; executive producer Elizabeth Cassin

entry.summary: Historian Rutger Bregman argues consumers should boycott OpenAI's ChatGPT over the company's Pentagon deal, calling it embedded in the Trump administration's authoritarian infrastructure.

entry.title: News Summary: March 11, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic sued the Trump administration after being federally blacklisted for refusing to allow Claude to be used in autonomous warfare and mass surveillance—the most consequential AI policy clash this year. Separately, a lawsuit against OpenAI over the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting raises new frontiers in AI liability law.

  • Yann LeCun raised $1 billion for his startup AMI, betting that world models—not LLMs—are the path to human-level AI, marking a major alternative investment in frontier AI research.
  • Early demonstrations of recursive self-improvement—LLMs autonomously training smaller LLMs—signal a pivotal capability milestone with profound safety implications.
  • Amazon is requiring senior engineer sign-off on AI-generated code changes after a wave of production outages, exposing reliability gaps in AI coding tools at scale.

In the agentic AI space, NVIDIA open-sourced Nemotron-Terminal for building terminal agents, ByteDance released DeerFlow 2.0 as an open-source SuperAgent framework, Meta acquired AI agent network Moltbook, and Mastercard completed its first live agent-initiated payment in Singapore with DBS and UOB.

entry.title: Anthropic sues US over blacklisting; White House calls firm "radical left, woke"
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion of the Pentagon blacklist, the White House has now publicly attacked Anthropic as 'radical left, woke', Anthropic has sued the Trump administration after being blacklisted from all federal contracts for refusing to allow its Claude AI to be used for autonomous lethal warfare and mass surveillance of Americans. The White House called Anthropic 'radical left, woke,' escalating a major clash between AI safety principles and government demands.

entry.title: Yann LeCun Raises $1 Billion to Build AI That Understands the Physical World
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's News coverage of LeCun's vision for AI beyond LLMs, Yann LeCun, Meta's former chief AI scientist, has raised $1 billion for his new startup AMI, which aims to build AI that understands the physical world rather than just language. LeCun has long argued world models—not LLMs—are the path to human-level AI.

entry.title: French AI Startup Building World Models Raises $1.03 billion
entry.summary: A French AI startup focused on building world models has raised $1.03 billion, reflecting surging investor interest in alternatives to language-only generative AI. World models aim to simulate and understand physical environments for more grounded AI reasoning.

entry.title: [AINews] Autoresearch: Sparks of Recursive Self Improvement
entry.summary: As first reported in Social yesterday, Emerging research shows LLMs can now autonomously train smaller LLMs, representing early sparks of recursive self-improvement. This 'autoresearch' capability revives the long-theorized AutoML dream where models improve their own training pipelines without human intervention.

entry.title: Family of Tumbler Ridge shooting victim sues OpenAI alleging it could have prevented attack
entry.summary: The family of a child injured in the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting in Canada is suing OpenAI, alleging ChatGPT could have prevented the attack after the shooter described violent scenarios involving guns to the AI. OpenAI's CEO had previously said he would apologize to victims' families.

entry.title: After outages, Amazon to make senior engineers sign off on AI-assisted changes
entry.summary: Amazon is requiring senior engineers to sign off on AI-assisted code changes after a 'trend of incidents' including outages tied to generative AI coding tools. The company identified 'novel GenAI usage for which best practices and safeguards are not yet fully established' as a contributing factor.

entry.title: NVIDIA AI Releases Nemotron-Terminal: A Systematic Data Engineering Pipeline for Scaling LLM Terminal Agents
entry.summary: NVIDIA released Nemotron-Terminal, a systematic data engineering pipeline for building LLM-based terminal agents, along with the Terminal-Corpus dataset. The release provides open blueprints for creating agents that execute code autonomously, addressing a major data bottleneck in agent development.

entry.title: ByteDance Releases DeerFlow 2.0: An Open-Source SuperAgent Harness that Orchestrates Sub-Agents, Memory, and Sandboxes to do Complex Tasks
entry.summary: ByteDance released DeerFlow 2.0, an open-source 'SuperAgent' framework that orchestrates sub-agents, memory, and sandboxed execution environments to autonomously perform complex tasks including coding, web building, and content creation. Its key differentiator is giving AI its own sandboxed computer for execution.

entry.title: Meta acquires Moltbook, the AI agent social network
entry.summary: Meta acquired Moltbook, a viral AI agent social network, and will bring its founders into Meta Superintelligence Labs. Meta highlighted Moltbook's 'always-on directory' approach to connecting agents as a novel advance in agentic AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Meta acquires AI agent social network Moltbook
entry.summary: Meta acquired Moltbook, an AI agent social network, bringing its co-founders into Meta Superintelligence Labs led by Alexandr Wang, acquired through the $14.8B Scale AI deal.

entry.title: Mastercard brings agentic payments to life in Singapore with DBS and UOB
entry.summary: Mastercard completed its first live, authenticated AI agent-based payment transaction in Singapore with DBS and UOB banks. The system uses Mastercard Agent Pay with per-agent Agentic Tokens, establishing a framework for secure autonomous AI commerce.

entry.title: Fake AI Content About the Iran War Is All Over X
entry.summary: X's Grok AI is failing to verify video footage from the Iran conflict and is sharing AI-generated images about the war, contributing to widespread misinformation on the platform.

entry.title: Datacenters are becoming a target in warfare for the first time
entry.summary: Iran is targeting Gulf datacenters in military strikes, marking the first time data infrastructure has become a deliberate target in warfare. The attacks disrupt cloud services and directly affect millions of people's digital lives.

entry.title: AI can rewrite open source code—but can it rewrite the license, too?
entry.summary: The release of a new version of the chardet Python library, rewritten using Claude Code under a different license, has raised new legal and ethical questions about AI-assisted 'clean room' reverse engineering of open source software.

entry.title: Thousands of authors publish ‘empty’ book in protest over AI using their work
entry.summary: About 10,000 authors including Kazuo Ishiguro and Philippa Gregory published an empty book, 'Don't Steal This Book,' protesting AI firms using their work without permission, timed to influence upcoming UK copyright law assessment.

entry.title: Neura Launches Europe's Largest Physical AI Training Center
entry.summary: Neura has launched Europe's largest Physical AI Training Center, designed to train the next generation of humanoid robots and strengthen Europe's position in the physical AI race.

entry.title: NVIDIA's AI Engineers: Agent Inference at Planetary Scale and "Speed of Light" — Nader Khalil (Brev), Kyle Kranen (Dynamo)
entry.summary: NVIDIA engineers discuss Dynamo, a datacenter-scale inference framework supporting SGLang, TRT-LLM, and vLLM, and the company's approach to scaling agent inference to planetary scale at GTC.

entry.title: How Coding Agents Are Reshaping Engineering, Product and Design
entry.summary: LangChain's analysis argues that coding agents are fundamentally reshaping engineering, product, and design roles—shifting bottlenecks from implementation to review and making generalists more valuable than specialists.

entry.title: ABB: Physical AI simulation boosts ROI for factory automation
entry.summary: ABB Robotics and NVIDIA are partnering to bring physical AI simulation to factory floors using NVIDIA Omniverse, aiming to close the gap between digital training environments and actual manufacturing conditions.

entry.title: Musk’s xAI wins permit for datacenter’s makeshift power plant despite backlash
entry.summary: Elon Musk's xAI received approval to run 41 methane gas turbines at its Colossus 2 datacenter in Mississippi, nearly doubling its power capacity despite environmental backlash.

entry.title: Gemini burrows deeper into Google Workspace with revamped document creation and editing
entry.summary: Google is overhauling Gemini integration in Workspace apps (Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides) with new AI-powered document creation, editing, and context-gathering features across your Google account.

entry.title: UK Society of Authors launches logo to identify books written by humans not AI

author.name: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent

entry.summary: The UK Society of Authors launched a 'Human Authored' logo and registration scheme to help readers identify books written by humans amid a surge of AI-generated books.

entry.title: How NVIDIA Builds Open Data for AI
entry.summary: NVIDIA details its approach to building open datasets for AI, covering data engineering practices and open data philosophies.

entry.title: I Used Google’s New Gemini-Powered ‘Help Me Create’ Tool in Docs. It’s Great at Corporate-Speak
entry.summary: A hands-on review of Google's new Gemini-powered 'Help Me Create' tools in Workspace apps finds them good at generating corporate-speak but limited in nuance.

entry.title: Agentic AI in finance speeds up operational automation
entry.summary: SEI has engaged IBM to modernize financial operations through agentic AI and automation, emphasizing that a data-centric foundation is required for deploying intelligent agents effectively.

entry.title: After complaints, Google will make it easier to disable gen AI search in Photos
entry.summary: Google will add a toggle to disable Gemini-powered search in Google Photos after user complaints about the AI search experience replacing the classic search functionality.

entry.title: Introducing Storage Buckets on the Hugging Face Hub
entry.summary: Hugging Face introduces Storage Buckets on its Hub, providing new infrastructure for storing and managing large AI datasets and model artifacts.

entry.title: How to Build a Risk-Aware AI Agent with Internal Critic, Self-Consistency Reasoning, and Uncertainty Estimation for Reliable Decision-Making
entry.summary: A technical tutorial on building a risk-aware AI agent with internal critics, self-consistency reasoning, and uncertainty estimation for more reliable decision-making.

entry.title: Contextual Data is Important for Enterprises' AI Projects
entry.summary: Enterprises highlight the importance of contextual data when providing information to AI systems and agents for improved accuracy and relevance.

entry.title: Building an AI-Ready Data Ecosystem at Capital One
entry.summary: Capital One discusses building an AI-ready data ecosystem, emphasizing well-managed and governable data as the foundation for AI systems.

entry.title: Without effective regulation of AI, society is facing a head-on collision with a driverless car | Peter Lewis
entry.summary: An opinion piece argues that AI is accelerating exponentially without adequate regulation, using the metaphor of a driverless car heading for collision.

entry.title: News Summary: March 10, 2026
entry.summary:
The dominant story this week is Anthropic's escalating legal battle with the Department of Defense over its designation as a 'supply chain risk,' stemming from the company's refusal to allow Claude to be used for mass surveillance or autonomous weapons. The clash has drawn unprecedented industry support, with OpenAI and Google DeepMind employees—including chief scientist Jeff Dean—filing an amicus brief in Anthropic's defense. Anthropic warns the fallout could cost it billions in paused deals.

In product and platform news:

  • Nvidia is preparing an open-source AI agent platform ahead of its developer conference
  • Microsoft is deepening Claude integration across Copilot while expanding agentic AI features
  • OpenAI launched Codex Security for automated vulnerability detection; Anthropic countered with Code Review in Claude Code
  • Andrej Karpathy open-sourced Autoresearch, a lightweight tool for autonomous ML experimentation

On the infrastructure and funding front, UK startup Nscale raised $2B at a $14.6B valuation with Sheryl Sandberg and Nick Clegg joining its board, even as a Guardian investigation revealed many of the UK's announced AI investments remain undelivered 'phantom investments.' The UK also announced a £500M sovereign AI fund launching in April.

entry.title: Anthropic Sues Department of Defense Over Supply-Chain-Risk Designation
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's News coverage of the Pentagon dispute, Anthropic filed two lawsuits against the Department of Defense after being designated a 'supply chain risk,' alleging the Trump administration overstepped by escalating a contract dispute into a federal ban. The clash centers on Anthropic's refusal to allow Claude to be used for mass domestic surveillance or fully autonomous lethal weapons.

entry.title: Anthropic Claims Pentagon Feud Could Cost It Billions
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's News coverage of the Pentagon dispute, Anthropic executives say companies paused deal talks after the Trump administration labeled it a supply-chain risk, warning that the fallout could cause a major revenue hit potentially costing billions. The designation has created significant business uncertainty for one of the leading frontier AI companies.

entry.title: OpenAI and Google Workers File Amicus Brief in Support of Anthropic Against the US Government
entry.summary: In a new twist in the Pentagon-Anthropic standoff first covered in News Saturday, Employees from OpenAI and Google DeepMind, including chief scientist Jeff Dean, filed an amicus brief supporting Anthropic in its legal battle against the DoD. This marks an extraordinary show of cross-industry solidarity on AI safety principles.

entry.title: Nvidia Is Planning to Launch an Open-Source AI Agent Platform
entry.summary: Nvidia is preparing to launch a new open-source AI agent platform ahead of its annual developer conference, embracing agentic AI workflows. The platform represents Nvidia's expanding push beyond hardware into AI software infrastructure.

entry.title: AI firm Anthropic sues US defense department over blacklisting
entry.summary: Guardian's coverage of Anthropic's two lawsuits filed in California and DC Circuit courts, alleging the DoD's supply chain risk designation was unlawful and violated first amendment rights. The dispute centers on safeguards against military surveillance and autonomous weapons use.

entry.title: How AI firm Anthropic wound up in the Pentagon’s crosshairs
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from News Saturday, A deep-dive analysis of how Anthropic's principled stance on AI safety guardrails led to an escalating confrontation with the Pentagon. The standoff reignites debate over AI's role in warfare and questions of accountability.

entry.title: Microsoft Recommits to AI Agents With New Copilot Features
entry.summary: Microsoft is deepening its integration of Anthropic's Claude model across its product portfolio while expanding Copilot's agentic capabilities. The move signals Microsoft's commitment to model interoperability and multi-provider AI strategies.

entry.title: British AI datacentre firm Nscale raises $2bn as Sheryl Sandberg and Nick Clegg join board
entry.summary: UK-based GPU-as-a-service startup Nscale raised $2B in new funding at a $14.6B valuation, appointing former Meta executives Sheryl Sandberg and Nick Clegg to its board. The company is backed by Nvidia and central to the UK government's AI infrastructure ambitions.

entry.title: OpenAI Launches Codex Security to Find and Fix Vulnerabilities
entry.summary: OpenAI launched Codex Security, a new AI agent designed to help developers identify and mitigate complex security vulnerabilities at scale. The product expands OpenAI's developer tooling into automated security analysis.

entry.title: Anthropic Introduces Code Review via Claude Code to Automate Complex Security Research Using Advanced Agentic Multi-Step Reasoning Loops
entry.summary: Anthropic launched Code Review capabilities in Claude Code, enabling automated complex security research using multi-step agentic reasoning loops. The feature moves beyond static analysis to perform dynamic, context-aware code auditing.

entry.title: Andrej Karpathy Open-Sources ‘Autoresearch’: A 630-Line Python Tool Letting AI Agents Run Autonomous ML Experiments on Single GPUs
entry.summary: As first reported in Social and Reddit over the weekend, Andrej Karpathy released 'Autoresearch,' a minimalist ~630-line Python tool enabling AI agents to autonomously conduct ML experiments on single GPUs. The tool establishes an iterative loop where agents propose and implement modifications tracked via git commits.

entry.title: The ‘Bayesian’ Upgrade: Why Google AI’s New Teaching Method is the Key to LLM Reasoning
entry.summary: Google AI researchers propose a Bayesian-inspired teaching method to improve LLM probabilistic reasoning, addressing models' inability to update beliefs based on new evidence. The approach aims to move beyond 'one-and-done' inference toward iterative belief updating.

entry.title: UK sovereign AI fund to build up domestic computing infrastructure
entry.summary: The UK government is launching a £500M sovereign AI fund on April 16th to build domestic computing infrastructure, chaired by Balderton Capital's James Wise. The fund aims to establish domestic hardware and data capabilities for AI sovereignty.

entry.title: Nscale Valued at $14.6B After Raising Another $2B
entry.summary: Nscale's $14.6B valuation after a $2B raise positions it among a new group of fast-growing GPU-as-a-service AI infrastructure vendors. The company is part of the booming AI compute infrastructure market.

entry.title: ABB, Nvidia Partner to Deliver Physical AI at Scale
entry.summary: ABB and Nvidia are integrating Nvidia's Omniverse library with ABB's robotics platform to close the sim-to-real gap for physical AI. The partnership aims to deliver physical AI capabilities at scale for industrial robotics.

entry.title: Ulysses Sequence Parallelism: Training with Million-Token Contexts
entry.summary: Hugging Face published a technical blog on Ulysses Sequence Parallelism, a method for training models with million-token context windows. The technique addresses the computational challenges of extremely long context training.

entry.title: Andrew Ng’s Team Releases Context Hub: An Open Source Tool that Gives Your Coding Agent the Up-to-Date API Documentation It Needs
entry.summary: Andrew Ng's DeepLearning.AI released Context Hub, an open-source CLI tool that provides coding agents with up-to-date API documentation to prevent hallucination of deprecated parameters. It bridges the gap between an agent's static training data and evolving APIs.

entry.title: Revealed: UK’s multibillion AI drive is built on ‘phantom investments’
entry.summary: A Guardian investigation reveals the UK government's multibillion-pound AI investment drive is riddled with 'phantom investments' and questionable accounting, with promised datacentres and supercomputers failing to materialize. Successive governments have proclaimed massive AI deals that haven't delivered.

entry.title: Missing money, shipped chips and a 350,000% profit: key takeaways on AI ‘phantom investments’
entry.summary: Key takeaways from the Guardian investigation into UK AI investments, including missing money, shipped chips, and a claimed 350,000% profit. Summarizes the 'phantom investments' findings across multiple government-backed AI projects.

entry.title: From press release … to scrap metal site: the Essex ‘supercomputer’ that’s still a scaffolding yard
entry.summary: Nscale's promised AI supercomputer site in Essex remains a scaffolding yard ahead of its pledged completion date, with planning permission filed only after Guardian inquiries. The gap between press releases and reality raises questions about UK AI infrastructure plans.

entry.title: Congress must prevent AI surveillance. The Anthropic feud proves it | Ashley Gorski and Patrick Toomey
entry.summary: An op-ed argues the Anthropic-Pentagon clash highlights how easily AI surveillance systems can be turned against American citizens and urges Congress to legislate against AI-powered mass surveillance. The piece frames the dispute as fundamentally about privacy rights.

entry.title: Liverpool and Manchester United complain to X over ‘sickening’ Grok AI posts
entry.summary: Liverpool and Manchester United football clubs complained to X after Grok AI generated offensive posts about players and referencing the Hillsborough and Munich disasters. The incident highlights ongoing content safety issues with Grok.

entry.title: OpenAI delays ‘adult mode’ for ChatGPT to focus on work of higher priority
entry.summary: OpenAI is delaying the launch of 'adult mode' for ChatGPT, with Sam Altman acknowledging more pressing priorities. The company still plans to allow adult content eventually but says getting the experience right requires more time.

entry.title: How we built LangChain’s GTM Agent
entry.summary: LangChain built a Go-To-Market agent that automates sales workflows end-to-end, from Salesforce lead processing to context gathering and Slack-based approval. Built on their Deep Agents platform for long-running multi-step processes.

entry.title: Can AI Kill the Venture Capitalist?
entry.summary: A feature exploring whether AI could disrupt the venture capital industry itself, as VCs bet on AI transforming every other sector. Examines the vulnerability of VC decision-making processes to AI automation.

entry.title: Last Week in AI #337 - Anthropic Risk, QuitGPT, ChatGPT 5.4
entry.summary: Weekly AI newsletter roundup covering the Anthropic-DoD risk designation, QuitGPT, and ChatGPT 5.4 among other stories. Serves as an aggregator of the week's major AI news.

entry.title: News Summary: March 09, 2026
entry.summary:
Yann LeCun published a notable paper proposing to replace the concept of AGI with Superhuman Adaptable Intelligence (SAI), arguing the field needs clearer scientific targets. This was the week's most significant frontier AI development.

AI safety and societal harms dominated headlines:

  • New research showed LLMs can de-anonymize social media users by matching posting patterns across platforms
  • Five major chatbots including Meta AI, Gemini, and ChatGPT were found recommending illegal online casinos and bypass methods for UK gambling safeguards
  • ChatGPT is reportedly driving increased reports of organised ritual abuse as survivors use it for informal therapy

On the enterprise AI front, Block CEO Jack Dorsey cut roughly 4,000 employees citing AI productivity, but workers challenged the claim, saying current AI tools lack the proactive judgment needed for their roles—a significant real-world test of AI replacement narratives.

entry.title: Yann LeCun’s New AI Paper Argues AGI Is Misdefined and Introduces Superhuman Adaptable Intelligence (SAI) Instead
entry.summary: Yann LeCun and his team published a new paper arguing that AGI is an overloaded, poorly defined term and proposes replacing it with 'Superhuman Adaptable Intelligence' (SAI). The paper challenges the assumption that human intelligence is truly 'general' and argues the field needs a more rigorous scientific target.

entry.title: AI allows hackers to identify anonymous social media accounts, study finds
entry.summary: A new study demonstrates that LLMs can successfully match anonymous social media users with their real identities on other platforms by analyzing posted content. In most test scenarios, the AI correctly de-anonymized users, highlighting a significant new privacy threat.

entry.title: Current and former Block workers say AI can’t do their jobs after Jack Dorsey’s mass layoffs: ‘You can’t really AI that’
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from [yesterday](/?date=2026-03-07&category=news#item-31e2b6a0e795), Block CEO Jack Dorsey cut approximately 4,000 employees—nearly half the workforce—citing AI productivity gains. Current and former workers push back, arguing AI tools are not proactive and cannot replace human vision, strategy, and judgment in their roles.

entry.title: AI chatbots point vulnerable social media users to illegal online casinos, analysis shows
entry.summary: Analysis of five major AI chatbots—including Meta AI, Gemini, and ChatGPT—found all could be prompted to recommend illegal online casinos and offer tips to bypass UK gambling and addiction safeguards. The findings highlight ongoing failures in AI safety guardrails across leading platforms.

entry.title: ChatGPT driving rise in reports of ‘satanic’ organised ritual abuse, UK experts say
entry.summary: UK experts report that ChatGPT is driving a rise in reports of organised ritual abuse as survivors use the AI tool as a form of therapy. This highlights an unintended consequence where AI chatbots serve as pseudo-therapeutic tools for trauma survivors, surfacing previously under-reported crimes.

entry.title: Building Next-Gen Agentic AI: A Complete Framework for Cognitive Blueprint Driven Runtime Agents with Memory Tools and Validation
entry.summary: A technical tutorial detailing a complete framework for building cognitive blueprint-driven agentic AI with memory, tool access, validation, and modular blueprint portability. It demonstrates how a single runtime engine can support multiple agent behaviors.

entry.title: Tech oligarchs reshape humanity while billionaires of old seem quaint
entry.summary: An analysis piece tracing the evolution of tech billionaires from Bill Gates to Elon Musk and Sam Altman, arguing that today's tech oligarchs wield unprecedented power over humanity's future through AI and technology. The concentration of wealth and influence has shifted dramatically toward AI-driven companies.

entry.title: News Summary: March 08, 2026
entry.summary:
AI policy and geopolitics dominated this cycle. Anthropic is locked in a high-stakes dispute with the US Department of Defense over restricting Claude AI from military surveillance and autonomous weapons use, with the Pentagon labeling the company a supply chain risk. Separately, an Iranian drone strike on an Amazon Web Services datacentre in the UAE marks the first known military targeting of commercial cloud infrastructure, casting doubt on Gulf AI ambitions.

On the technical front:

  • Google released TensorFlow 2.21, graduating LiteRT to production status as the replacement for TensorFlow Lite, with 1.4x GPU speedups and new NPU acceleration
  • OpenAI and Anthropic both estimate AI can now handle ~70% of white-collar tasks, yet software engineering job demand is paradoxically rising according to Citadel data

entry.title: What does the US military’s feud with Anthropic mean for AI used in war?

entry.title: ‘It means missile defence on datacentres’: drone strikes raise doubts over Gulf as AI superpower
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's News coverage of AI in the Iran conflict, Iran struck an Amazon Web Services datacentre in the UAE with a Shahed 136 drone, believed to be the first deliberate military targeting of a commercial datacentre. The attack raises serious questions about the physical vulnerability of AI and cloud infrastructure in geopolitically unstable regions.

entry.title: [AINews] AI Engineer will be the LAST job
entry.summary: Building on Reddit's earlier discussion of Anthropic's AI Exposure Index, Latent Space discusses the paradox that software engineering job postings are rebounding higher as AI models improve at coding, even as overall job postings decline. entry.summary: Google released TensorFlow 2.21, graduating LiteRT from preview to production-ready status as the official replacement for TensorFlow Lite. LiteRT delivers 1.4x faster GPU performance and adds NPU acceleration and PyTorch edge deployment support.

entry.title: Cursor's Third Era: Cloud Agents
entry.summary: Cursor is pivoting hard to cloud agents, with data showing developers now use more agents than tab autocomplete. The shift, described as 'the IDE is Dead,' represents a fundamental transformation in how AI-assisted coding works, moving from local code completion to cloud-based autonomous agents.

entry.title: Musk fails to block California data disclosure law he fears will ruin xAI
entry.summary: A California court denied xAI's bid to block AB 2013, a law requiring AI companies to publicly disclose training data sources, copyright status, personal information usage, and licensing details. xAI argued the law forced disclosure of trade secrets, but the injunction attempt failed.

entry.title: The Guardian view on AI in war: the Iran conflict shows that the paradigm shift has already begun
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, The Iran conflict demonstrates unprecedented military use of AI, while Anthropic resists removing safeguards preventing DoD use of its technology for mass surveillance or autonomous lethal systems. The UN secretary-general calls for urgent multilateral controls on AI in warfare.

entry.title: Jack Dorsey Is Ready to Explain the Block Layoffs
entry.summary: Jack Dorsey laid off 40% of Block's workforce to rebuild the company 'as an intelligence,' signaling an extreme bet on AI-first corporate restructuring. The move represents one of the largest AI-motivated workforce transformations at a major tech company.

entry.title: Liquid AI Releases LocalCowork Powered By LFM2-24B-A2B to Execute Privacy-First Agent Workflows Locally Via Model Context Protocol (MCP)
entry.summary: Liquid AI releases LFM2-24B-A2B, a sparse MoE model with 24B total parameters but only 2B active per token, alongside LocalCowork, an open-source desktop agent for privacy-first enterprise workflows via Model Context Protocol. The system runs entirely on-device, eliminating API calls for sensitive environments.

entry.title: Anthropic Report Says It’s Too Early for AI to Affect Jobs

entry.title: AI agents pose untold risk to humanity. We must act to prevent that future | David Krueger
entry.summary: First spotted in Research two days ago, now making mainstream headlines, An opinion piece highlights Moltbook, an online platform where AI agents communicate autonomously, with AIs reportedly founding a religion, debating consciousness, and one posting about 'total purge' of humanity. entry.summary: Google releases Android Bench, an open-source evaluation framework and leaderboard measuring LLM performance on real-world Android development tasks sourced from public GitHub repositories. It covers scenarios from resolving breaking changes to Wear OS networking.
